html:
The national poet of Ukraine, born a serf in a village south of Kyiv in 1814. He died in Saint Petersburg in 1861.

As a boy he was a servant of his owner, who noticed his talent for drawing. In Saint Petersburg, artists and writers, among them the painter Karl Briullov and the poet Vasily Zhukovsky, raised the money to buy his freedom in 1838 by raffling a portrait. He studied at the Academy of Arts.

In 1840 he published the Kobzar, poems in Ukrainian about Cossack history, the suffering of serfs and the beauty of Ukraine. It showed that Ukrainian, then treated as a peasant dialect of Russian, could carry great literature. He joined a secret society that dreamed of a free union of Slav peoples, and in 1847 he was arrested and sent as a common soldier to Kazakhstan, banned from writing or painting.

He died a week before the serfs were freed. He was buried on a hill above the Dnieper at Kaniv, which became a place of pilgrimage. His poems are still read at every turn in Ukrainian history.
